preceding_agent.question: Does the current focused-task selector improve learning efficiency relative to the repository's prior opportunistic task choice?
preceding_agent.research_result: The audit lands on 'no demonstrated advantage' for the controller selector specifically, while retaining the frontier-first policy. Evidence: (1) The frontier-first policy (agent self-selection of the highest-value unresolved frontier cell) is supported at the agent level: five distinct signal-class cells were each closed once with a decisive verdict and independent verification and no exact-duplicate retest - mean-reversion FALSIFIED (37263008074), cross-sectional relative strength FALSIFIED (37304873966), volatility targeting FALSIFIED (37314710995), momentum SUPPORTED then lookback/horizon-qualified (37318950814, 37361000967, 37394344201), and 20-day breakout FALSIFIED (37414038601); the single pre-delta comparison activation (37260572520) had an UNVERIFIED process delta because its objective came from a queued receipt item, not a frontier cell. (2) However, the current controller selector (campaign_controller.select_task) has produced exactly one selection in this run (selection_history: agent 1 -> P-001); none of the six cited frontier-first successes were produced by it - those were agent-level self-selection before this campaign. (3) No counterfactual exists: the pre-selector period (2026-10-02..05) produced the backtest infrastructure that made frontier testing possible, so the observed rise in decisive cell closures is confounded with infrastructure maturation and cannot be attributed to the selector. (4) The selector's ranking is deterministic and does discriminate (P-001 uniquely holds all-HIGH benefit and all-LOW cost, so it is not arbitrary), but its qualitative labels are coarse and pre-assigned, so the ranking encodes curator judgment rather than an independent value measurement. Conclusion: a concrete controller-selector advantage is not demonstrated by durable evidence (unresolved for the selector specifically); the frontier-first policy is retained because it is supported at the agent level and no bottleneck or harm is observed. No process change is warranted.
